PullRequest.Title: copilot: remove unused code and orphaned dependencies
PullRequest.Body:
- Remove unused helpers, types, constants, internal methods, and legacy notebook-generation prompts from the built-in Copilot Chat extension.
- Remove internal production code referenced only by its own tests, including obsolete prompt rendering, indentation-tree utilities, an OpenAI simulation adapter, and diff-generation code, together with exclusive tests and fixtures.
- Delete obsolete tests and unused mocks and test helpers.
- Recursively prune orphaned telemetry and file-stat plumbing, replay timing infrastructure, folding bookkeeping, caches, state, dependencies, and configuration entries.
- Remove obsolete language-server context statistics and prompt telemetry metadata while retaining recording operation lookup with focused regression coverage.
- Remove orphaned parser query registrations and semantic-chunking code, unused TypeScript-context APIs, and obsolete session/worktree helpers.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve and submit a Copilot CLI chat prompt with file/diagnostic references
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Prompt reference resolution must finish before the request reaches the CLI session. URI translation may await filesystem stat calls; attachment construction then completes before submission.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat the candidate path in the isolated worktree before replacing a referenced URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one candidate stat per URI/diagnostic reference after the change, with references processed concurrently by Promise.all; effective cardinality scales with distinct prompt references.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same stat existed, and fallback matching could scan the primary plus every additional workspace; the diff narrows matching to the primary workspace only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each stat is awaited on prompt construction's critical path, although references run concurrently.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of prompt references and, before the diff, number of additional workspaces. The diff removes the additional-workspace multiplier.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reference translations run via Promise.all with no new limiter; the change decreases candidate workspace checks rather than increasing concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is used for candidate stats; warm operating-system filesystem caches may help. The diff does not invalidate or bypass a prior cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed signatures and translation loop directly remove additional workspace candidates while preserving the pre-existing stat.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reference counts and stat latency vary by local/remote filesystem, but the changed cardinality is lower than before.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; filesystem work and retained workspace metadata decrease.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create, update, and observe cloud-agent tasks or Chronicle cloud sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Live task operations await their HTTP requests. The removed task-update poller and removed session lookup/consent helpers are no longer on any reachable changed path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Previously polled getTask every two seconds for up to sixty seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to roughly 30 serialized GET requests per invocation before the diff; zero after removal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base revision contained the polling helper, but its interface and implementation are both deleted with no replacement call path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When invoked, polling delayed completion until a task update or timeout; the boundary is removed rather than moved.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Previously fetched one cloud session for reattach verification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One GET per invocation before the diff; zero after removal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The orphaned method performed a single GET and JSON parse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request would have been awaited by its caller; no replacement boundary is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of task-update waits or cloud-session verification attempts; changed reachable cardinality is zero for the deleted APIs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The old task poll loop was serialized per invocation; no new burst or replacement polling loop is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed positive, negative, or in-flight cache participates in these deleted calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that network boundaries are removed; high that no replacement boundary appears in the reviewed changed callers/interfaces.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The deleted methods appear orphaned, so actual prior production frequency may already have been zero.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the diff removes network operations and telemetry around them.

Scenarios.Scenario: Request inline completions and TypeScript language-server context while typing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Prompt/context collection and the existing tsserver/native TypeScript request must complete within the inline-completion budget before the model request proceeds. Changed telemetry and unused helper removal is off the authoritative context-computation path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute the existing typescript.tsserverRequest command for context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One in-flight context-population request per managed completion request, subject to the existing in-flight request manager and cancellation behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command and await existed before the diff with the same request count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing context computation remains on the completion critical path; the diff only removes unused request metadata and timeout-inspector events.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit the completion/model request after prompt construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged one logical model request per uncached completion flow, governed by existing completion caches and cancellation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The changed file only removes an unused parameter interface; fetch behavior is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This remains the dominant completion boundary and is not added or rescheduled by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Typing/completion request frequency, project size for TypeScript context, and diagnostic/log line count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing in-flight context request ownership, cancellation, and completion caching remain; no aggregate concurrency increase is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Runnable-result/context caches and ghost-text completion caches remain. Removed cache methods and outdated-state fields have no remaining callers; no changed code bypasses a live cache. Cold and warm request behavior is therefore unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the service diffs and surviving call paths: only unused metadata, events, and methods are removed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Project-size-dependent TypeScript work can be large, but no changed mechanism increases its frequency or scope.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; telemetry/allocation work is generally reduced and expensive IPC/network cardinality is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Index/search workspace files and replay or record workspace edits
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workspace search depends on existing file reads, parsing, and embedding/reranking. Recording/replay processes document events locally. Removed stat/version, semantic chunking, and simulated-time replay APIs have no replacement on the live path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Previously statted a file to derive a size-mtime version identifier.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stat per explicit helper invocation before the diff; zero after removal. No surviving caller uses the helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Filesystem and text-document representations exposed the stat-backed helper, including byte encoding for dirty documents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The boundary is removed, not shifted onto indexing or search.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Previously parsed source and ran semantic target tree-sitter queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One parse/query pass per helper invocation, scaling with source length; zero after deleting the orphaned API and query registrations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base exposed semantic chunk tree/name helpers that parsed the entire supplied source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No replacement parsing is introduced on workspace search or replay paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workspace file count, source bytes, and recording log entry count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing workspace search concurrency is unchanged; removed APIs cannot add subprocess, filesystem, or parser bursts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing parser/file indexing caches remain. The deleted fast-version API was not replaced with full reads, and removed recording lookup state had no surviving consumers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from deleted implementations and absent repository references.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace sizes vary widely, but all identified changed expensive work is removed or unreachable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; filesystem, parser CPU, and replay timer work decrease.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initialize a chat session with repository/worktree isolation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Primary-folder repository resolution, trust checks, Git status/migration, and worktree creation must complete before the isolated session starts. The diff deletes the unused multi-root initialization branch while leaving the primary path unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve repositories, inspect changes, create worktrees, migrate changes, and commit/checkpoint additional repositories through Git services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before deletion, up to one repository/status/worktree sequence per selected folder, with worktree creation and migration performed concurrently across trusted folders; zero for the deleted branch after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base implementation used Promise.all/Promise.allSettled across primary and additional folders and then persisted additional worktree metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations were awaited before multi-root session initialization; no replacement fan-out is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and update persisted session metadata for additional workspaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata read or sequenced write per explicit method invocation before deletion; zero afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Additional workspace metadata was read from or written to the existing session metadata file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Deleted metadata operations are not added to the primary session path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of selected workspace folders/repositories and modified files. Effective additional-workspace cardinality becomes zero.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The removed branch could burst worktree creation once per trusted repository via Promise.allSettled; the surviving primary path remains one repository at a time.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Primary session metadata caching/sequencing remains. Additional-workspace metadata storage and lookup are deleted together with their callers, so no cache miss fallback is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that subprocess/filesystem fan-out is deleted and primary-workspace behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The multi-root branch appears orphaned, making prior production frequency uncertain, but no surviving scenario gains work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; repository fan-out, metadata retention, and concurrent Git work decrease.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate the extension and construct tools, parsers, prompts, and notebook context
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Extension activation registers services and lazily constructs tools; prompt rendering occurs only when requested. Changed declarations, telemetry metadata, tests, and unused render/notebook helpers do not add startup work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Registered tool count, parser query set size, prompt item count, and notebook cell count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new task, worker, timer, queue, or eager construction is introduced; removed tool-extension and parser-query registrations reduce possible work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Lazy tool construction remains. Notebook/document and parser caches used by live paths remain; deleted snapshot/helper APIs have no callers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High after reviewing activation-adjacent registries, parser services, notebook helpers, and prompt renderers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact activation savings are not measured, but the direction of changed work is non-increasing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; startup and prompt-side allocation/registration work is unchanged or reduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full 375-file inventory and performance-relevant production hunks. The PR consistently removes orphaned helpers, telemetry, caches/accessors, parser queries, polling, metadata, and multi-root Git fan-out together with their callers. No changed path adds expensive work, increases effective cardinality/concurrency, defeats a live cache, or retains resources longer, so no finding or regression-fix record was warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
